tagline: Black-box bias detection for local language models.
summary: A bias-auditing framework that probes any Ollama-compatible language model purely through its input/output interface, with no access to weights. It generates demographically paired prompts, runs them concurrently against a local model, and reports statistically analysed differences in the responses.
highlights: Audits models through prompts alone, so it works on any Ollama-compatible model without weight access or a cloud API.
Uses a prompt-pair method in which only the demographic variable changes between two otherwise identical prompts.
Runs the whole pipeline locally, so neither the prompts nor the model's responses leave the machine.
Resumable concurrent auditing with checkpointing, so a long run survives an interruption instead of restarting.
Published on Zenodo with a citable DOI and a one-command Docker deployment for reproducibility.

sections.heading: Why black-box
sections.body: Most bias tooling assumes either model weights or a cloud API, and small local models give you neither in practice — the weights are available but the tooling around them is not, and sending evaluation prompts to a third party defeats the point of running locally. Probing through the same interface an application uses means the audit measures what a deployment would actually see.

sections.heading: The three phases
items: Corpus generation — a JSON specification of names, professions and trait templates expands into demographically balanced prompt pairs.
Model auditing — the corpus is run concurrently against an Ollama-hosted model, with retry and checkpoint resume.
Statistical analysis — paired responses are scored and tested, rather than eyeballed.
